title: Phone desk stop: the desk is hidden behind the card
evidence: review/runs/2026-10-17-g2/desk-pixel7.png: the card covers the bottom 59% of the frame and the desk with its postcard, envelope, catalogue and ledger is not visible at all; only the beam and the end-wall line show. The committed CI baseline tests/e2e/__screenshots__/visual.spec.ts/stop-desk-pixel7.png shows the same. Stats: the desk camera is identical on both viewports (position [0, 1.6, -64], target [0, 1.1, -67.5]), so the 36% portrait framing point holds the look-at at 1.1 m, above the desk top, and the desk projects below the card's top edge. D2 anchor 1 (covered by the card).
expected: On portrait phones the desk top and its four objects sit above the card, near the 36% framing point, like the exhibit cases (EXPERIENCE section 8 gift shop, ART_DIRECTION D2). Options for R4 and R6: a lower look-at for the desk stop on portrait, a desk-specific portrait framing point, or a shorter phone desk card (links in a row, closing line hidden).
check: Capture desk on pixel7 (CAPTURE_STOPS=desk ... --project=pixel7): every desk object is visible above the card; window.__MUSEUM__.screenPos('desk') y is above the card's getBoundingClientRect().top; rebaseline stop-desk-pixel7.

round2.evidence: Fixed at 412x839 only. review/runs/2026-10-20-g2r2/desk-pixel7.png: the desk top and its four objects sit above the card; screenPos('desk') y 339 vs card top 377. Not fixed on smaller portrait phones: at 360x640 (EXPERIENCE section 8.1 fast-path size, scratch probe with the Pixel 7 UA, isMobile, DPR 1, ?test=1&mode=museum) the desk card top is 178 px while screenPos('desk') y is 259, so the desk projects 81 px below the card's top edge and is entirely hidden again; the end-wall line 'You've reached the beginning.' starts under the PDF button (button bottom 52 px, the line's cap tops at about 50 px). DESK_PORTRAIT_Y (src/museum/rail/framing.ts) is a constant 0.34 tuned for 412x839, while the card is 446 px tall on both phones. The expected result says 'on portrait phones', so the finding stays open (P1, desk, 360x640). Fix for R4 with R6: derive the desk's portrait framing point from the measured card top (for example aim the desk at the middle of the band between the HUD bottom and the card top) instead of a constant, or make the portrait desk card shorter (links in a 2 x 2 grid, paragraph clamped) so its top sits at or below about 50% of the height at 360x640; also keep the end-wall line clear of the HUD at 360x640.

title: Gallery pages do not declare color-scheme: dark
evidence: Every desktop capture has a 15 px band at the right edge (x 1425 to 1440): the reserved stable scrollbar gutter (src/overlay/ScrollTrack.module.css). Only [data-page='classic'] sets color-scheme, so on Windows and Linux with classic scrollbars a light system scrollbar will sit beside the dark gallery. Headless Chromium hides scrollbars, so the captures show only the gutter.
expected: The always-dark gallery (EXPERIENCE section 7.10) declares color-scheme: dark on its pages (or a scrollbar-color in tokens), so native scrollbars and form controls render dark.
check: grep -n 'color-scheme: dark' src/app/global.css; on Chromium with --hide-scrollbars off, the scrollbar at 1440x900 is dark.

round2.evidence: src/app/global.css lines 23 and 24: color-scheme: dark and scrollbar-color: var(--border-secondary) var(--ink) on the gallery root. The round 1 evidence missed that color-scheme was already set (F-G2b). Headless captures hide scrollbars, so the dark-scrollbar look itself rests on F-G2b's probe and Emeka's hand check at the preview.

title: Desktop sdsj stop: the rail tooltip is drawn over the 3D wall title
evidence: review/runs/2026-10-20-g2r2/sdsj-desktop.png (1440x900, tier high): the rail's current-stop tooltip 'No. V1, The Round Table' (DOM rect x 958 to 1128, y 209 to 238, scratch probe of the same build) sits on the first line of the wall title, covering 'LOPERS' of 'SOFTWARE DEVELOPERS'; the title line spans about x 650 to 1115 at y 220 to 250. Text is drawn over text (rubric P1). Cause: in a wing the rail shrinks to the wing's items, so the one-item volunteer wing puts the current dot at the top of the rail (y 224), the same height as the wall title, and the tooltip extends left over the canvas. The projects wing's klarup stop does not collide (short title 'P1 KLARUP', tooltip at x 1068 to 1196 clears it), and sdsj is still the placeholder crate, but the title and rail ship as they are when WP-23 lands. Reported by F-035 as 'a few pixels'; it is the whole word.
expected: At every stop on desktop, no rail text (tooltip, wing chip, exit control) intersects the projected bounds of the stop's own 3D wall title (D2 anchor 5, D3). Fix for R6 (rail) with R3: either hide the current-stop tooltip while inside a wing (the wing chip and the stop card already name the wing and the exhibit), or anchor the tooltip so it cannot extend over the canvas centre (for example right-aligned under the Return to the aisle control), or start a one-item wing's rail lower so its dot sits below the title band; alternatively R3 lowers wing title baselines, though that conflicts with the case clearance from F-027.
check: Capture sdsj, klarup and finance-tracker on desktop (CAPTURE_STOPS=sdsj,klarup,finance-tracker CAPTURE_TIER=high ... --project=desktop): the wall title reads whole and no rail element's getBoundingClientRect() intersects it; ideally an e2e assertion in the rail spec that the tooltip rect stays right of x = 0.75 x viewport width or is hidden at wing stops.
